combined.semantics: Union of complete rectangular guide envelopes, not ink area. The enclosing bbox includes empty gaps and is reported separately. Available regions are not actual reserved layout bands.

guide_geometry.font_policy: Preserve configured legend font size; never shrink the canvas or quantitative size keys.
guide_geometry.selection_policy: Fit first, then declared candidate order; never minimize occupied area as an aesthetic objective. Automatic placement is provisional and needs visual judgment.
guide_geometry.measurement_note: Legend bbox includes rendered keys, labels and title. Available-region occupancy describes free space outside the plot, not allocated legend space. Ratios and pass status describe technical fit, not design improvement. Check other annotation collisions visually.

point_layout.pair_sample_definition: One-based parsed observation positions excluding the header; no observations are dropped.
point_layout.packing_origin: Category center plus point_category_offset; maximum spread is measured around that anchor.
point_layout.algorithm: Greedy nearest-center circle packing in final physical geometry; bounded least-crowded fallback grid when infeasible.
point_layout.note: Only categorical coordinates move. This arrangement is not a KDE/density estimate. Circle-circle spacing is audited; point-summary and text overlaps still need visual review. Explicitly enlarge the allowed lane/canvas or choose another reading task if circles cannot fit.

baseline_geometry.summary_raw_separation_note: Envelope crossings require visual inspection, particularly opaque points over box medians; violin contour width is a conservative envelope, not a density crossing test.

color_decisions.role_note: Categorical assignment follows the unchanged declared order. Raw observations use a supplied point color when present, otherwise the category mapping; neutral role assignments and single-quantity bars are EasyViz adaptations. No numeric scale or fitted line is inferred.

palette.name: notch2-balanced
palette.source: Cruz Tleugabulova et al., Nature Communications (2024), Figure 2b
palette.provenance: Selected and reordered four embedded PDF legend colors (I2, I1, I4, M1). This selection spans cell classes within the same figure and is not an author-provided named palette.
palette.note: User selected candidate B on the cell-atlas panel; review independently for other chart contexts.

candidates.reason: Category identity on raw observations; open neutral summaries/contours. Measured fit at the adopted science, canvas and fonts; explicit paths remain locked. This limited route is a proposal, not a preferred or exhaustive design.

mechanisms.observed: Repeated aligned plot boxes, shared labels and class blocks separate related populations.
mechanisms.adaptation: Compare an associated sample lane or shared-scale facets when overlay obscures the adopted comparison.
mechanisms.boundary: A neighboring lane is an adaptation; it must retain group association and numeric values, and cannot erase needed pairing.
mechanisms.evidence: Observed in the inspected supplied PDF; adaptations are proposed for new data. See references/literature-style.md.
reasons: Observed family/burden fit and adopted purpose fit

mechanisms.observed: One treatment pair occupies a narrow region with readable samples, summaries and uncertainty.
mechanisms.adaptation: Allocate width from actual mark/label capacity instead of stretching two categories across a broad canvas.
mechanisms.boundary: A narrow plot is useful only if labels and every observation still fit at the adopted size.
mechanisms.evidence: Observed in the inspected supplied PDF; adaptations are proposed for new data. See references/literature-style.md.
reasons: Observed data do not meet maximum_categories=2

mechanisms.observed: A wider declared curve and local white separation remain visible over tiny points.
mechanisms.adaptation: Give an existing summary enough local contrast or choose separate lanes rather than fading all data.
mechanisms.boundary: No curve/model is introduced; a contrasting under-stroke or raw lane is a task-specific adaptation.
mechanisms.evidence: Observed in the inspected supplied PDF; adaptations are proposed for new data. See references/literature-style.md.
reasons: Observed data do not meet dense_raw_layer=True

mechanisms.observed: Density silhouettes remain distinct from bounded inner summaries.
mechanisms.adaptation: Let the adopted density lead only when shape is part of the question; subordinate existing points/summaries without erasing them.
mechanisms.boundary: Density must already exist. Small or tied groups may not justify KDE; do not tune bandwidth for a prettier silhouette.
mechanisms.evidence: Observed in the inspected supplied PDF; adaptations are proposed for new data. See references/literature-style.md.
reasons: Observed data do not meet kind=violin

mechanisms.observed: Fine neutral density contours, categorical areas and definite inner summaries coexist in compact groups.
mechanisms.adaptation: Emphasize the adopted summary; raw points and area-color reassignment are explicit adaptations.
mechanisms.boundary: Preserve quartiles, KDE and bandwidth; adding an inner summary requires separate adoption.
mechanisms.evidence: Observed in the inspected supplied PDF; adaptations are proposed for new data. See references/literature-style.md.

mechanisms.observed: A tall expression matrix retains its few columns as compact reading units.
mechanisms.adaptation: Plan cell width/height and label capacity from matrix shape before choosing the ramp.
mechanisms.boundary: Square cells are optional. Preserve values, ordering and normalization; few columns should not become decorative horizontal ribbons.

mechanisms.source: PROGENy Fig. 2b,c, PDF p. 4; Vanneste Fig. 4d, PDF p. 6
mechanisms.observed: Separators vary with cell density; dense tiny-cell heatmaps do not frame every cell equally.
mechanisms.adaptation: Use subordinate seams for large direct-lookup cells; reserve enough physical space for adopted value labels.
mechanisms.boundary: A seam policy is conditional. Colors cannot invent a meaningful center, endpoints or missing-state meaning.
mechanisms.evidence: Observed in the inspected supplied PDF; adaptations are proposed for new data. See references/literature-style.md.
reasons: Does not address the adopted reading task

mechanisms.observed: Uniform gray bars or decoded black/white/gray compositions have definite boundaries.
mechanisms.adaptation: Use labels/positions to decode a single quantity; reserve categorical colors for a required second variable.
mechanisms.boundary: Multiple series need distinct decoding; neutral is optional, and supplied project colors remain authoritative.
mechanisms.evidence: Observed in the inspected supplied PDF; adaptations are proposed for new data. See references/literature-style.md.
reasons: Does not address the adopted reading task

mechanisms.source: scWAT Fig. 3g,m, PDF p. 5; Vanneste Fig. 2g,h, PDF p. 4
mechanisms.observed: Tight within-category series and wider category gaps repeat with a compact shared guide.
mechanisms.adaptation: Plan stroke clearance, series gap and category pitch separately; adapt the data region to the real comparison.
mechanisms.boundary: Do not copy a source aspect ratio, axis break, reference value or significance layer.
mechanisms.evidence: Observed in the inspected supplied PDF; adaptations are proposed for new data. See references/literature-style.md.
reasons: Need observed multiple_series before this mechanism's applicability is established

mechanisms.source: scWAT Fig. 2c,i,j, PDF p. 4; Vanneste Fig. 2e–h, PDF p. 4
mechanisms.observed: Open bars, small observations and visible uncertainty endpoints remain associated.
mechanisms.adaptation: Plan bar width, sample span and intervals together; open or filled summaries depend on the leading layer.
mechanisms.boundary: Summary and uncertainty meanings must already be adopted; hollow is not a universal style.
mechanisms.evidence: Observed in the inspected supplied PDF; adaptations are proposed for new data. See references/literature-style.md.

mechanisms.observed: Blue/pink observations and fitted strokes differ from the blue/coral bar treatment elsewhere on the page.
mechanisms.adaptation: Choose class colors on actual small marks and keys; a usable area palette need not work for tiny points.
mechanisms.boundary: A scatter needs a relationship question; a fitted line requires an adopted model. Source hues are not compulsory.
mechanisms.evidence: Observed in the inspected supplied PDF; adaptations are proposed for new data. See references/literature-style.md.
reasons: Need observed grouped_scatter before this mechanism's applicability is established
